title: Vexana: Absent
dateline: Selrick Academy, the observation lab. Before dawn.
mood: Before dawn a far star over the bay begins to flash, and so does the small gold star at Guinevere’s collar.

hero.alt: A tall tower with a long glass lab across its top stands under heavy storm clouds; then, inside the glass lab, Guinevere has her eye to a telescope while Ruby and Angela wait behind her.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: The storm that began at dusk had not stopped. Lightning split the clouds over the bay. In the glass lab at the top of the tower, not one screen flickered.
The lamp beside the telescope was lit. It had been lit most nights since Guinevere first climbed up here. The wind threw rain across the glass in front of it.
She had her eye to the lens. On the first two nights Ruby and Angela had asked her to leave. After that they kept the tower’s sensor array running, and nobody touched the lamp.
Her fingers went to the small gold star at her collar, the Emblem of Hope. It was lit.
It had been lit in Angela’s hands too, weeks ago, on a lab bench, while Ruby ran code to make it a tracker. Near or far, the glow never changed.
“It only says yes,” Ruby had said.
“Then yes is something,” Angela had said.
Since then Guinevere had watched the sky. In the last week a faint point of light had come out over the bay, past the dome’s seaward edge. The students called it the Singularity now.
The night log lay open beside Ruby’s console, in Guinevere’s hand. Most lines said one word:
Nothing.
The last few said
Point over the bay. Faint. No change.
Angela knelt at an open panel of the array, her cat-ear headset pushed back, a tool in her hand. Since the point came out, the array’s readings over the bay had not held still.
“Ruby, the energy readings here are still unstable. The repair process is going slowly.”
“Keep going,” said Ruby from the console.
In the lens, the faint light changed. It burned magenta. It had four points, and it was flashing.

media.alt: Through the round lens of the telescope, a four-pointed star of magenta light burns in the storm clouds above a dark ridge.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: Guinevere held very still. Her breath fogged the eyepiece. She wiped it with her thumb and looked again.
“It’s flashing...” She did not look away. “Could it be Vexana?”
Angela’s tool stopped. Ruby bent over the screen linked to the telescope, one eye behind her visor. A trace spiked across it, then spiked again, higher.
“Based on the energy waveform, it’s likely an Ender,” said Ruby. “The energy fluctuation from the chest area... is exceptionally powerful. I think it’s trying to lure us in.”
The star at Guinevere’s collar glowed gold under her fingers. It did not flicker.
“Guinevere,” said Ruby. “I said lure.”
“I heard you.”
“Then you know what it is.”
“I know what you read.” Guinevere kept her eye on the far star. “I don’t know what it is.”
Ruby looked at her a moment longer. Then she saved the trace and sat with her gloved hand flat over it on the screen. Angela did not pick her tool back up.
Guinevere pulled the night log over. Under the last
No change,
she wrote
Flashing.
Then she put her eye back to the lens.
In the lens, the star flashed, and flashed.
The classroom. Morning.
The storm had thinned to gray. Under the billboard of her and Vexana in the courtyard, Guinevere had touched her collar, as every morning. Lit.
Now she sat in the second row. Vexana’s desk beside hers was empty. Nobody had sat in it since.
Its chair stood square to the desk, the way Vexana had always left it. Guinevere straightened it herself each morning, before anyone could knock it crooked.
In the front row, Selena held her phone sideways. Over her shoulder its screen showed the Academy feed: the point over the bay, a graph climbing. She jerked back. Her pen dropped. Her papers flew.

media.alt: Selena in her school uniform starts back from the phone she holds sideways, her mouth open, her pen dropping and her papers flying around her desk.

segs.t: “If the world ends now, what about my graduation?!” said Selena.

blocks.caption: If the world ends now, what about my graduation?!

segs.t: The class laughed. Even the teacher’s mouth twitched.
Guinevere did not laugh.
You wouldn’t have either,
she told the empty chair.
You’d have looked at me, to see if I did.
Then she watched the window.
Between first and second class, students crowded the corridor under the hologram wall. A boy read from his tablet.
“Detecting an abnormal signal from the Singularity. Energy fluctuations are highly unstable. It could be an Ender invasion.”

media.alt: Students in navy blazers crowd a bright corridor between classes; Guinevere stands among them beside a black-haired boy.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: “Wonder what the Aspirants plan to do...” said a girl beside him, and glanced at Guinevere.
The wall showed the day’s attendance record, a long list of names in white. Guinevere passed it at this hour every day. She stopped at the same line.
Vexana: Absent, in red.
The Academy’s files said Missing. The wall said only
Absent
Absent,
she would think, and touch her collar.
Not here yet.
Then she walked on.
This morning she read the word. She touched her collar.
The Emblem was flashing.
It flashed under her fingers, bright, then brighter, over and over. The beep had not come once since the day Vexana was taken. It did not come now.
She stood in the middle of the crowd and could not move. Gold light came through her fingers in pulses, onto the red word on the wall.

media.alt: Guinevere stands before the glowing hologram wall, which reads Vexana: Absent, the small gold star at her collar shining.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: Weeks,
she thought.
Weeks of nothing. And now you.
Not here, then. But close. Out there, where the far one flashed.
Her voice came out loud in the crowded corridor.
“The emblem... it’s flashing. It’s Vexana... she must be at the Singularity. I have to go find her.”

Nobody answered. The students looked at the star at her collar, and then looked away. The boy put his tablet in his bag. Low, behind her, someone said, “She still thinks that thing means she’s alive.”

Guinevere went to the corridor window. Below it the dome curved down to the waterfront, pale against the gray. Past its edge, the small magenta star hung over the bay in the thinning storm. She counted its flashes against the ones under her fingers.
You always came to me,
she thought.
Every time. This time I’m coming to you.
The far star flashed in time with the one at her collar. As she watched, its four points began to pull apart.
